quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Always identify yourself and help at the scene of an accident.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object.
questions.explanation: A cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road. Always be careful when passing bicycles.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Prepare to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and with caution. Check both directions before entering.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if safe to do so.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: How long does it take a fully loaded truck to stop at 55 mph?

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Large trucks need much longer to stop than cars. A fully loaded truck may need almost 400 feet to stop at 55 mph.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is nearby.

questions.question: The traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach. What should you do?

options.text: Continue through the intersection with caution.
Stop immediately.
Stop before entering unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the light turns red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light, slow down and stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do if there are two railroad tracks side by side?

options.text: It is always safe to cross after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing.
When one train passes, check the other track before crossing.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one train passes, check the other track before crossing.
questions.explanation: After one train passes, watch for a second train on the other track. Always make sure no train is coming on either track before you cross.

questions.question: What does it mean when a driver extends their left arm upward?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm upward, they are signaling that they plan to turn right. Watch for this signal from other drivers.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should turn into:

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to where you came from. This keeps you safe when turning.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with speed and road conditions. Steering ability does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: Which of the following should drivers NOT do?

options.text: Dim headlights when within 200 feet of oncoming traffic.
Use parking lights only when parked.
Dim headlights when following within 200 feet of another vehicle.
Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid glare from oncoming headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dim headlights when within 200 feet of oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Dim your headlights when within 500 feet of oncoming traffic and when following within 200 feet of another vehicle. Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid bright headlights. Use parking lights only when parked.

questions.question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep the same speed on the exit ramp.
Pass slower vehicles on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp. Then slow down to a safe speed for leaving the freeway.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels straight.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb when parking downhill. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic and toward the curb.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch out for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss than cars. They can hide in blind spots. It is hard to judge distance and speed of motorcycles. Always be alert and careful around motorcycles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
Construction zone is ending.
School crossing ahead.
Person with flag directing traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Person with flag directing traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area. Follow their directions.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be treated as:

options.text: Safe, since trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Always treat railroad crossings as dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs and signals. Only cross when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When parked facing downhill, your front wheels should point:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Toward the curb.
Away from the curb.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the curb.
questions.explanation: Point your wheels toward the curb when parked downhill. If your brakes fail and the car rolls, it will roll away from traffic and toward the curb.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Turn left because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in the direction of the arrow. But oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and all pedestrians first.

questions.question: You must yield to other drivers:

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do before you move your car?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check if the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check if the way is clear.
questions.explanation: When backing up, look through your back window for people and objects. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially around children. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing into or out of a driveway.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach their destination more quickly.
Follow other cars more closely.
Stay farther behind other cars.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: When driving on wet roads, increase the distance between your car and the car in front of you.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants toward the left. This means:

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will need to turn left soon.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the road edge shows where the road boundary is. If the line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two lanes of traffic are about to become one lane.
